text: The completeness axiom that distinguishes the real numbers from the rationals states that:
choices: Between any two distinct real numbers there lies a rational number
Every Cauchy sequence of rational numbers converges to a rational number
Every nonempty set of reals that is bounded above has a least upper bound in R
Every bounded sequence of reals is monotone
explanation: The completeness (least-upper-bound) axiom says every nonempty bounded-above set of reals has a supremum in R; this is exactly what Q lacks. The statement about Cauchy sequences of rationals is false, since such a sequence can converge to an irrational like sqrt(2). Density of Q and the false monotonicity claim are unrelated properties.
